body:
## Summary

On a dtplyr input, a factor column carrying a declared `NA` level loses it when
`nest_with_margins()` folds it into `.key`. The same call on the same data
through the local `data.frame` backend keeps it, so the nested column's domain
differs by backend with no error, warning, or other diagnostic.

This is the residual of #415, which widened the encode-and-rebuild route to the
columns a verb's result carries *as columns of its own* — a fixed `.by` key, or a
column `expand_with_margins()` passes through. A nested payload column is not one
of those: it crosses the branch union like every other column, but by the time
`finalize_margin_operation()` runs it is inside a cell, where
`restore_margin_factors()` has nothing to rebuild.

## Reproduction

```r
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

data <- data.frame(
  passthrough = structure(
    c(1L, 2L),
    levels = c("a", NA_character_),
    class = "factor"
  ),
  group = factor(c("g1", "g2")),
  value = 1:2
)

nested <- function(input) nest_with_margins(input, .grouping = rollup(group))

cat("nest payload -- local:  ")
print(levels(nested(data)$data[[1]]$passthrough))
cat("nest payload -- dtplyr: ")
print(levels(as.data.frame(collect(nested(dtplyr::lazy_dt(data)))$data[[1]])$passthrough))
```

## Observed / Expected

Observed, verbatim, at `7e26f4e` (the head of #415's branch):

```
nest payload -- local:  [1] "a" NA
nest payload -- dtplyr: [1] "a"
```

Expected: the dtplyr line prints `[1] "a" NA`, as its local line does, with
`is.na()` on the cell's column agreeing between the two.

## Root cause

The same one as #408 and #415: `data.table`'s rbind drops a declared `NA` level
from the result and turns the values that used it into missing codes.

`nest_margin_pipeline()` hands `carried_columns = function(data_vars, plan) plan$by`
to `prepare_margin_operation()`, and the comment there says why: the encode arm of
`label_margin_branch()` and the rebuild in `restore_margin_factors()` are two halves
of one route, and encoding a column the finalizer cannot reach would leave it as
character — strictly worse than the level it loses today.

## What was unmeasured

All three items are measured; the results are in the comment below, and the
prototype there is green under the full suite. In summary: the rebuild goes
before `nest_expanded_margins()` folds the cell, because the dtplyr union turns
the values on the declared level into genuine missing before any fold, so an
in-cell rebuild has nothing to rebuild from; `.keep = TRUE`'s copies take the
same loss, and so does the nested copy of a *grouping* column carrying an NA
level, whose outer column #415 restores while its cell copy keeps the character
domain; and `nest_by_with_margins()` does not differ.

The comment's *Acceptance* section is what this issue is done against.

comments.body:
Measured the three open items at `40697b1`, the head of #415's branch. All three
are answered, and the first one settles the fix's shape.

## 1. Where a payload column can be rebuilt: before the fold

The two candidates are not alternatives. The loss is already complete at the
union, before anything folds a cell:

```r
lv <- structure(c(1L, 2L), levels = c("a", NA_character_), class = "factor")
a <- dtplyr::lazy_dt(data.frame(k = 1L, p = lv))
b <- dtplyr::lazy_dt(data.frame(k = 2L, p = lv))
u <- dplyr::collect(dplyr::union_all(a, b))
```

```
levels: [1] "a"
values: [1] "a" NA  "a" NA
is.na:  [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
```

The values that used the declared `NA` level come back as genuine missing, so a
rebuild inside the summary expression has nothing to rebuild from — it would
restore the level and leave every value on it missing. The encode arm is
required wherever the rebuild sits, and the only remaining question is where to
put the rebuild call.

A `dplyr::mutate()` over `pick(everything())` does translate under dtplyr, so
the in-cell rebuild is available; it is just an extra expression inside a
data-masked summary buying nothing over one call on the expanded step. Rebuild
before `nest_expanded_margins()`.

## 2. `.keep = TRUE`'s copies: yes, and the loss is wider than stated

The copies take the same loss, and so does something the issue did not name:
the nested copy of a *grouping* column carrying a declared `NA` level. The outer
column is restored by #415's fix while the cell's copy of it is not, so one call
returns the same column with two different domains:

```
NA-level group outer local:   [1] "g1" NA "Total"
NA-level group outer dtplyr:  [1] "g1" NA "Total"
NA-level group cell  local:   [1] "g1" NA
NA-level group cell  dtplyr:  [1] "g1"
```

The copies are made in `execute_margin_nest()` under internal names after
`prepare_margin_operation()` built `column_info`, so they are in no
`factor_info` entry and the encode arm never sees them.

## 3. `nest_by_with_margins()`: no difference

As expected. It shares `nest_margin_pipeline()` and loses the payload level
identically; only the cell's class differs (`data.table` rather than `tbl_df`,
because it collects).

## Prototype

Measured rather than proposed. Four changes, and the full suite is green under
them (`testthat::test_local()`, 0 failures):

1. `nest_margin_pipeline()`'s `carried_columns` becomes
   `function(data_vars, plan) data_vars` — every input column reaches the
   result, as an outer column or inside the cell.
2. `execute_margin_nest()` synthesizes a `factor_info` entry per `.keep` copy
   from the source column's, with `col` swapped for the internal name, and
   hands the extended `column_info` to `expand_margin_union()`. A copy carries
   no Margin label, so it takes the `encode_missing_label` route already there
   and is rebuilt on its declared levels with none appended.
3. `restore_margin_factors()` runs on the payload columns of `expanded`, before
   `nest_expanded_margins()` folds them.
4. `nest_margin_pipeline()` narrows `operation$column_info$factors` to the outer
   columns before `finalize_margin_operation()`, so the finalizer does not
   `mutate()` a column that is now inside a cell.

The comment on `carried_columns` in `nest_margin_pipeline()` states the rule
this changes and is rewritten with it.

## Acceptance

For a `dtplyr` input, on both `nest_with_margins()` and
`nest_by_with_margins()`, with `.keep` either value: every factor column inside
a `.key` cell has the levels and the `is.na()` pattern its local `data.frame`
counterpart has. A `.keep = TRUE` copy of a grouping column is rebuilt on its
declared levels with no Margin label appended, which is what the local backend
answers.

title: dtplyr nest payload drops a declared NA factor level inside its cell
